The [[Liga Super]] champions for 2012 was [[Kelantan FA|Kelantan]]. ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division. {{col-begin|width=auto}} {{col-break}} ===To Malaysia Super League=== '''Promoted from [[2011 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[PKNS F.C.|PKNS]] * [[Sarawak FA|Sarawak]] '''invited team''' * [[LionsXII]] {{col-break|gap=3em}} ===From Malaysia Super League=== '''Relegated to [[2012 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[Pahang FA|Pahang]] * [[Perlis FA|Perlis]] '''Exchanged with Lions XII to [[S. League]]''' * [[Harimau Muda A]] {{col-end}} ==Teams== A total of fourteen teams will contest the league, including eleven sides from the [[2011 Liga Super|2011 season]] and two promoted teams from the [[2011 Liga Premier]]. [[Singapore Lions]] of [[Football Association of Singapore|Singapore]] will also participate in the 2012 season, replacing [[Harimau Muda A]]. [[Perlis FA|Perlis]] and [[Pahang FA|Pahang]] were relegated at the end of the [[2011 Liga Super]] after finishing the season in the bottom two places of the league table. [[2011 Liga Premier]] champions [[PKNS F.C.|PKNS]] and runners-up [[Sarawak FA|Sarawak]] secured direct promotion to the Liga Super. Following an agreement between the [[Football Association of Singapore]] and the [[Football Association of Malaysia]], [[Young Lions (football team)|Young Lions]], with most of the members of the squad are players from Singapore's national under-23 team, will replace [[Harimau Muda A]], which represent the Malaysian Under-23 national football team. While the [[Singapore Lions]] will compete at the [[Liga Super]], [[Harimau Muda A]] will take the [[Young Lions (football team)|Young Lions]] position in the [[S. League]].{{cite web|publisher=TODAYonline|title=Singapore to field a team in M-League, Piala Malaysia|url=http://www.todayonline.com/Sports/EDC110712-0000140/Singapore-to-field-a-team-in-M-League,-Malaysia-Cup|access-date=12 June 2011}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite web|agency=Bernama|title=Harimau Muda to play in S-League, Young Lions in Malaysia's Liga Super|url=http://www.bernama.com.my/bernama/v5/newsgeneral.php?id=600787|access-date=12 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120603165507/http://www.bernama.com.my/bernama/v5/newsgeneral.php?id=600787|archive-date=3 June 2012|url-status=dead}} Young Lions was later replaced by a new team, named [[LionsXII]] that will replace the former under-23 football team.[http://www.fas.org.sg/news/fas-reveal-lionsxii-coach-and-squad-list FAS Reveal Coach and Squad list for LIONSXII] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107054722/http://www.fas.org.sg/news/fas-reveal-lionsxii-coach-and-squad-list |date=7 January 2012 }} Retrieved at 5 December 2011 fromFootball Association of Singapore * [[Felda United F.C.|Felda United]] * [[Johor FC]] * [[Kedah FA|Kedah]] * [[Kelantan FA|Kelantan]] ([[2011 Liga Super]] champions) * [[Kuala Lumpur FA|Kuala Lumpur]] * [[Negeri Sembilan FA|Negeri Sembilan]] * [[Perak FA|Perak]] * [[PKNS F.C.|PKNS]]¹ * [[Sabah F.C.
